newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia lists 25 properties for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia lists 25 properties for privatisation.

text.p: Mongolia has listed 25 state-owned properties around the capital of Ulan Bator for auction in July, the State Property Commission said on Tuesday.

The downtown Youth Hotel, a property with more than 30 rooms, would be offered in an auction open to Mongolian or foreign buyers at a starting price of 779.32 million tugriks ($976,609), the commission said.
Offices, a former school and a 864-square metre (9,300-square ft) shop with a starting price of 199.00 million tugriks would also be offered at separate auctions in the month, it said.
The starting price of the shop has been cut by half since auctioneers failed to sell it in June, it said.
The state would auction two unfinished buildings in Nalaikh town, 40 km (25 miles) east of Ulan Bator, it said.

Western diplomats say the victory of ex-communist N. Bagabandi in Mongolia's May presidential election could slow the country's privatisation drive, but officials said the July auctions had been previously approved and would be unaffected.
